MECHANICAL CHARACTERIZATION 5.1 Polymer Composites In this study, two different polymer composite materials namely 20% wt CF/ABS and 40% wt. CF/PA66 were used for the compression overmolding on metal inserts. The panels made up of both these materials are individually tested under tension to determine the base material characteristics in both along the bead and in perpendicular directions. Type 4 tensile specimens as per ASTM D638 were machined from the AM- CM panels and tested at 5 mm/min in a universal tensile testing machine with strain extensometers. The tensile characteristics of the 20% wt. CF/ABS AM-CM panel are shown in Fig. 5.1.1. The average tensile strength along the bead is 63.35 +/- 9.44 MPa while the average tensile strength perpendicular to the bead is 33.77 +/- 8.3 MPa. Figure 5.1.1. Stress-strain characteristics of 20% wt. CF/ABS in perpendicular the bead and along the bead directions. The tensile characteristics of the 40% wt. CF/PA66 AM-CM panel are shown in Fig. 5.1.2. Microstructure Characterization The microstructure of as printed and compressed preforms were investigated in this subsection. A Keyence 7000 optical microscope was used to analyze the 2-layer AM Preform microstructure before and after compression. A total of twelve samples were analyzed – six across the bead path and six along the bead path as shown in the Fig. 5.1.3. Additive manufacturing of preforms leads to high porosity within the beads as evident by the absorption of the potting resin with the microstructure of these samples (refer Fig 5.1.3 (b)). The sample sets (1-1 to 1-3 and 2-1 to 2-3) exhibit similar features across the bead path at different locations. A high percentage of fibers are observed to be at the intersection of the beads and aligned along the bead path as highlighted by orange outline boxes in Fig. 5.1.4 (a).
